messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@acme.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Mar 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: context-length profiling + next steps

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for taking the call earlier today. Quick recap and the concrete asks so we can put together a pricing estimate: 

1) Workload profile (you mentioned a few variants today):
   - Short assist/chat: typical prompt size ~120 tokens, completion ~220 tokens, high frequency (70% of calls)
   - Doc summarization: avg prompt ~6k tokens (multi-doc), completion ~400 tokens, intermittent (20% of calls)
   - Long-context extraction: single-doc heavy context ~30k tokens, completion ~600 tokens, low traffic (10% of calls)

2) Monthly volume estimate: you gave a ballpark of ~150M generation tokens across product usage (prompt+completion combined) and ~20M embedding tokens for searches. Please confirm.

3) Target unit economics/budget: you mentioned a target of $X-$Y per 1M tokens — can you share a target $/1M tokens or an annual budget range so we can propose profiles (batching, quantization, cache) that meet that?

4) Context length needs: please confirm whether 8k contexts are sufficient for doc summarization use cases or if 32k/128k class contexts are required for a non-trivial portion of traffic. That affects model choice and pricing heavily.

Next steps: if you can reply with a short token profile table (avg prompt tokens, avg completion tokens, percent of traffic per profile) we'll convert that into a unit-cost estimate ($/1M tokens) across 8k/32k/128k options and recommended optimizations (prefetching, KV cache, batching).

I attached a simple CSV template (acme_token_profile.csv) you can paste into. Happy to hop on a quick 20m call if that's easier.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Samir Shah <samir@acme.ai>

Date: Fri, 26 Mar 2027 17:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: context-length profiling + next steps

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the recap. Below is the token profile based on the last 30 days of telemetry (rough averages):

- Short assist/chat: avg prompt 110 tokens, avg completion 240 tokens, ~72% traffic
- Doc summarization: avg prompt 5,800 tokens, avg completion 420 tokens, ~18% traffic
- Long-context extraction: avg prompt 31,200 tokens, avg completion 650 tokens, ~10% traffic

Monthly volumes (approx):
- Total generation tokens (prompt+completion): 150,000,000 tokens/month
- Embedding tokens (search/metadata): 20,000,000 tokens/month

Budget target: leadership is expecting a target around $250–$400 per 1M tokens for production inference (this includes model and infra; they want to understand what is feasible).

Context needs: doc summarization can fit into 8k if we chunk/stream, but quality drops and engineering overhead increases. The long-context extraction requires at least 32k for reasonable fidelity; a small subset (~2% of long-context) truly needs 128k (very large manuals). Overall: 18% of traffic prefers 8k/32k mix, 10% needs 32k+, with ~2% of total needing 128k.

I've attached the filled CSV. Let us know the cost scenarios and any tradeoffs (latency vs cost).

Best,
Samir
Head of AI Platform, Acme
samir@acme.ai

Attachment: acme_token_profile.csv (filled)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@acme.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Mar 2027 09:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: context-length profiling + next steps

Samir —

Appreciate the detailed numbers — super helpful. Attached is a concise pricing estimate (redwood_pricing_estimate.pdf) and the assumptions used. High-level summary here so you can share with leadership quickly: 

Scenario A — Cost-optimized (prefer 8k where possible, aggressive batching & cache)
- Assumes doc summarization chunked to 8k, long-context fallbacks to hybrid retrieval + short generation
- Estimated blended unit cost: $210 / 1M tokens
- Expected avg p99 latency: short assist 80–120ms, doc summarization 400–650ms
- Notes: additional engineering to chunk and stitch, minor quality degradation for some summaries

Scenario B — Balanced (mix 8k + 32k for doc summarization)
- Use 32k for doc summarization, 32k for most long-context extractions
- Estimated blended unit cost: $315 / 1M tokens
- Expected avg p99 latency: short assist 90–130ms, doc summarization 450–800ms
- Notes: better quality, moderate infra cost, recommended for initial GA

Scenario C — Fidelity-first (support 128k where required)
- Support 8k for short, 32k for most docs, 128k for the critical subset (~2% of traffic)
- Estimated blended unit cost: $460 / 1M tokens
- Expected avg p99 latency: short assist 100–160ms, long-context 900ms–1.5s
- Notes: highest cost but preserves fidelity; recommend for legal/regulated workflows where docs cannot be chunked

Unit economics & assumptions (short):
- Token accounting: billable units = prompt + completion tokens returned
- Batching: assumptions include continuous batching for high-frequency short assists (reduces per-token overhead)
- Cache: KV prefix caching for repeated prompts reduces effective token generation by ~6–12% on targeted flows
- Quantization: x8-bit model variants reduce GPU costs; we factored in a 15–25% cost improvement where quality tolerates it

Next steps:
- If leadership is comfortable with Scenario B as a starting point, we can prepare an SOW and a 30-day pilot (we’ll instrument cost/latency dashboards + eval sets).
- If you want a deeper breakdown, I can produce a per-profile cost table ($/1M tokens) for 8k/32k/128k and an ROI sheet vs your budget target.

Would you prefer Scenario A (aggressive cost) or Scenario B (recommended)? I can loop in Solutions Eng to scope the pilot once you confirm.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_pricing_estimate.pdf (summary + assumptions)

From: Samir Shah <samir@acme.ai>

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear scenarios. Leadership reviewed and favors Scenario B to start (balanced). They want the pilot to include:

- 30-day pilot with telemetry (cost, tokens, latency)
- Guardrails: per-route rate limits and a fall-back policy to cheaper model variant if budgets exceed threshold
- Evaluation: a small eval set of 120 prompts for doc summarization and 30 prompts for long-context extraction to measure quality delta vs chunking

Please send an SOW and a pilot checklist. We want kickoff next Wed if possible.

Samir
